title: stakeholder-briefing-poc-synthesis-and-convergent-recs
executive_summary: High-level readout from the 3-week POC with Nimbus Retail (search + summarization use case). Core finding: Redwood runtime with KV-prefix caching and a small dedicated pool of A100-equivalent capacity meets Nimbus' latency SLOs at ~45% lower unit token cost vs their current hosted provider when using dynamic batching and quantized 4-bit model variants. Customer confidence increased after two successful production-like runs, but they require clarified data controls and a staged fallback plan before moving off pilots.
content:
Purpose:
This doc synthesizes technical outcomes, business impact, and recommended next steps following the Nimbus Retail POC (search + product-summary assistant). It is intended for GTM, product, and engineering stakeholders to converge on an operational deployment path and an executive-approvable ask.

What we ran:
- Workload: user search queries (median length 26 tokens), catalog summarization for product pages (avg 420 tokens).
- Models tested: open-llama-13b (fp16), redwood-multi-variant-7b-q4 (4-bit), redwood-fallback-6b.
- Infra: hosted API baseline, dedicated pool (2 x A100 equiv), KV-prefix cache enabled on serving runtime, continuous batching window 15ms.
- Success criteria: p50 text gen latency < 120ms for search, p95 < 900ms for summarization; per-100k-token cost <= $35; no data exposure incidents.

Key metric outcomes:
- Latency: search p50 = 87ms (dedicated), p95 = 210ms; summarization p50 = 340ms, p95 = 780ms.
- Throughput: dedicated pool sustained 150 qps of short-queries with batch occupancy ~18 tokens/request on average.
- Cost: estimated steady-state token cost on dedicated = $22 / 100k tokens (including amortized infra & cache benefits); hosted baseline equivalent from Nimbus vendor = $40 / 100k tokens under similar QoS constraints.
- Quality: ROUGE-L on summarization testset maintained parity (+/- 0.8 points) between 4-bit and fp16 variants in human blind eval of 120 samples.
- Reliability: 3 failover trials exercised fallback to redwood-fallback-6b with controlled degradation (latency +70%, content quality reduced but acceptable for fallback).

Customer sentiment snapshot:
- Product: excited about cost delta and latency improvements; concerned about auditability/KMS integration for PII handling.
- Infrastructure: prefers a staged hybrid approach rather than immediate cutover; asked for a dedicated staging VPC with audit logs export for 90 days.

Deployment recommendation (convergent path):
1) Phase 1 (staged production): Provision a Dedicated pool sized at 3x of POC baseline (to cover 99th percentile spikes) inside Nimbus-managed VPC with private connectivity. Configure KV-prefix caching with prewarm on catalog ingestion and dynamic batching at 15ms window. Route 10% of production traffic for 4 weeks (canary) with automatic rollback policy.
2) Phase 2 (scale & harden): Expand dedicated pool + autoscaling policy, integrate customer KMS for envelope encryption of audit logs and request metadata, enable token-level cost telemetry in Console.
3) Phase 3 (SLA): If Phase 2 meets SLOs for 30 days, sign a 12-month dedicated commitment with burst credits and SRE runbook handover.

Risk summary and mitigations:
- Data controls: Customer requires stricter controls around PII. Mitigation: deploy in VPC with KMS, redact identified PII at ingestion, and send signed artifacts to customer audit logs.
- Model regression on long-tail prompts: Mitigation: maintain model-variant fallback and add regression monitoring for flagged prompt sets; weekly eval cadence for first 8 weeks.
- Cost overruns during spikes: Mitigation: autoscaling policy with cost-threshold alarms and burst-to-hosted fallback disabled unless manually enabled.
- Operational runbook gaps: Mitigation: create a 5-runbook bundle (incidents, rollout, cache invalidation, quantization rollback, billing reconciliation) as part of Phase 1 deliverables.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (approval): contract addendum for staging VPC and 3-node Dedicated pool (2 weeks procurement lead).
- Week 1–2: infra build, KMS integration, SSO access provisioning, runbook drafts.
- Week 3–6: canary rollout (10% traffic), weekly evaluation checkpoints, adjust cache profiles.
- Week 7–8: full ramp to 50–70% contingent on SLOs, finalize enterprise terms.

Resource estimate (rough):
- Engineering: 2 SEs (6 weeks), 1 SRE on-call partial (8 weeks), 1 infra engineer (2 weeks) — estimate 280 person-hours.
- Infra: dedicated nodes (3 x A100 equiv), expected monthly infra delta to customer ~$13k/month (est).
- Support: 1 solutions success manager for onboarding (4 weeks).

deployment_recommendation: Primary: Dedicated pool in Nimbus VPC with KV-prefix caching, quantized model variant as main serving instance, fp16 variant as on-demand heavy-quality path.
Fallback: redwood-fallback-6b automatically applied when latency or memory pressure observed, with circuit-breaker to prevent cascading failures.
Operational controls: KMS-backed audit logs, 90-day log retention (customer request), token-level cost telemetry enabled for initial 60-day window.
risk_and_mitigations: PII handling gap — use customer KMS and ingestion redaction pipeline; provide proof-of-encryption before canary
Quality drift on long-tail prompts — weekly regression tests and immediate rollback criteria defined
Unexpected cost spike — autoscaler with hard cost limit + manual override for bursts

2026-02-22 to 2026-03-21: 4-week canary at 10% with weekly checkpoints
